title: dedicated autoscaler: smoother burst controls and utilization reporting (v32)
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: Reduce noisy scale-ups during short traffic spikes while preserving sustained throughput guarantees for Dedicated fleets and provide clearer utilization telemetry. This PR implements a token-bucket smoothing layer for burst allowance, migrates autoscaler decision logic to use p95 sustained-utilization windows, and adds new utilization metrics and dashboards. Key changes: 1) Autoscaler: add token-bucket smoothing with configurable refill and windowed p95 measurement for sustained capacity decisions; 2) Metrics: expose dedicated.burst_allowed_tokens, dedicated.burst_used_tokens, dedicated.sustained_util_p95, dedicated.queue_latency_p95 to telemetry; 3) Config: extend fleet autoscaler config schema (v2) with burst_smoothing_enabled, burst_token_rate, sustained_window_secs and safe defaults to preserve backwards compatibility; 4) Rollout: feature-flagged, canary rollout plan (5% -> 25% -> full) with automatic rollback on increased tail-latency or error-rate; 5) Tests & perf: unit and integration tests added plus perf-canary load tests showing ~35% reduction in reactive scale-ups and 12% improvement in p99 queue latency for short spikes. Backwards compatibility and migration: new schema is optional; legacy fleets without v2 config continue to use previous behavior. Operational notes: new dashboards (telemetry/rows) and alerts added for sustained_util_p95 and burst_token_depletion to detect starvation. See release notes and rollout checklist below.

review_comments: Brendan Lee: Overall looks good. Can you explain the choice of p95 over p90 for sustained_util? Concerned about sensitivity to outliers.

Aisha Khan: We chose p95 because our production analysis showed p95 better captures sustained pressure for multi-tenant fleets; p90 reacts too quickly to brief microbursts. Added comments and test cases demonstrating differences.

merge_details: Merged by Marta Ruiz after approvals from Brendan Lee and Connor Patel. Canaries started at 2026-02-18T03:00:00Z.
release_notes: Autoscaler: added optional burst_smoothing using token-bucket (configurable).
Autoscaler: use p95 sustained-util window for scale decisions to reduce noisy scale-ups.
Telemetry: new metrics emitted - dedicated.burst_allowed_tokens, dedicated.burst_used_tokens, dedicated.sustained_util_p95, dedicated.queue_latency_p95.
Config: autoscaler schema v2 introduced (backwards compatible).
Operational: dashboards and alerts added for burst token depletion and sustained utilization regressions.
testing_notes: Unit tests cover token bucket race and refill semantics.
Integration tests run against a mocked fleet show stable behavior under synthetic spikes.
Perf-canary load tests validated reduction in reactive scale-ups and improved queue tail latency before global rollout.
Canary rollout plan: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback if p99 queue latency increases >10% or error rate increases >0.5%.
Observed results: ~35% fewer reactive scale-ups and ~12% p99 queue latency improvement on short bursts in perf environment.
notes: No breaking changes for fleets that do not opt-in to the v2 config.
Operators should monitor new metrics and ensure alert thresholds are tuned for their workload mix.
Followup work planned: adapt autoscaler heuristics for cold-start scenarios and add per-customer burst budgets.
